title: Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection
description: The built-in dependency injection container for ASP.NET Core and generic hosts.

data.text: Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection is the built-in IoC container for ASP.NET Core. It supports constructor injection, service lifetimes (Singleton, Scoped, Transient), and open/closed generic registration.

data.title: Service Registration

terms.definition: One instance for the entire application lifetime.
A new instance every time it is requested.

data.title: Caution
data.text: Avoid injecting scoped services into singletons - it causes scope validation errors.

The lifetime decides how often an instance is constructed. A singleton is created once for the whole application, a scoped service once per request, and a transient service every time it is requested. Getting this wrong causes one of two bugs: shared mutable state leaking across requests, or a memory leak from services that are never released.

data.title: Registering each lifetime
Interview angle: the captive dependency
data.text: A singleton that depends on a scoped service captures it for the lifetime of the application, so the scoped service is never released and is shared across requests. In Development, `ValidateScopes` throws a clear error; in Production the default host also validates scopes. The rule to state in an interview is that a service may only depend on another service with an equal-or-longer lifetime: singleton depends on singleton, scoped depends on scoped or singleton, transient depends on anything.

data.title: Key Takeaways
data.takeaway: Dependency Injection is fundamental to building testable and maintainable .NET apps.
